method: Six study nodes x the ten IEC 61882 guide words; adversarial verification of the six highest-severity rows; synthesis; referee.

rows.deviation: The proposed fixed anchor (H* = min of the seven online last-finalized heights, B* = its hash) is directionally right but, AS STATED, is vacuous for the rejoin property: it requires no post-reconnect progress, and it detects a fork only at or below H*. It can pass with the victim ~20 heights behind the group, which is exactly the gap the failed run showed.
rows.cause: H* is min of the seven at healing start, so B* is the oldest shared head, not the group's head. In the observed cycle the online group was ~48 at healing start while the victim was later 56-63 and the group 67-69; the anchor block at 48 was already passed by the victim at about +66 s. is_finalized is membership in the seen-closure of the latest fringe (block-storage/src/dag/representation.rs:61-67,141-143), a property inherited by every descendant, so a divergent branch ABOVE H* still answers true. The retained finalized_marker(H*, required=True) only tests height >= H* (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:150), i.e. the oldest online head. The current-but-racy target is max of the seven (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:183); the proposed min is lower still, so the gate is weaker than the code it replaces.
rows.consequence: FALSE PASS. A victim that is still partitioned but reachable, that never syncs, or that forked above H* passes on the first poll after connect. The fix cures the false FAIL of AG-01 by weakening the criterion until a stale-history read satisfies it, and the published 'unanimous finalized height/hash' claim becomes stronger than what was checked. This is the classic criterion drift: the acceptance bar moves to whatever the harness can certify.
rows.current_behaviour: Proposed only; today's code uses max-of-seven plus exact equality (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:85,183-185). Under the proposal the healing wait would pass as soon as all eight answer is-finalized(B*) and every last-finalized height is >= H*, with no requirement that the victim reach or follow the group.
rows.safeguard: Keep is-finalized(B_min) as the SAFETY anchor, then add a fixed POST-RECONNECT target for LIVENESS, both monotone: (1) after network connect, submit one signed deploy and require its block finalized (is-finalized(post_hash) true) on all eight — this is fork-sensitive above H* and cannot be satisfied by pre-partition history; or, with no production desired, require every node's last-finalized height >= H_heal_max = max of the seven at healing start (the pre-888a0b92c target, git show 888a0b92c^:tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py). (2) Bound the remaining lag by measurement: require victim LFB >= group median - (observed group spread + system finality lag + pre-registered margin), where the spread is max-min among the seven at the pass sample and the finality lag is 4 in the recorded A2.2 witness (docs/src/spec/testnet-acceptance.md:2006). (3) Record B*, H*, the sample time and the seven rows in the result. Bound: the post target is frozen; lag = spread + 4 + margin, all measured, not a constant.
rows.formalizable: Law 15 supplies only monotonicity; 'finalizing a pre-event anchor implies rejoin' has no theorem and is refuted by the run itself (the victim passes a block it already had, or the slowest of seven, while the group is 20 heights ahead). Owed candidate law with that witness: 'A fixed anchor at or below every participant's pre-event last-finalized block is invariant under non-participation after the event.' The fresh post-reconnect block is the only predicate here that is both monotone and fork-sensitive above the anchor.
rows.falsifier: A synthetic victim that answers is-finalized(B*) true but is denied all new blocks must FAIL the fixed gate (it passes the proposed one). Replaying the failing run must not pass at the first poll; it must require the post-reconnect block or H_heal_max.
rows.cost: ~2 days including the post-reconnect deploy path and the lag recorder.

rows.deviation: The healing window is a fixed 150 s reused for four different waits, with no measured catch-up rate. The tolerance is more permissive than any measurement supports, so it cannot distinguish a slow runner from a broken node, and 'scale from the victim gap' without a rate is a guess.
rows.cause: tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:131 sets args.window=150; comments at :24-27 and :158-160 justify 150 and 300 as 'pre-registered' bounds but cite no measurement. Drill.wait uses the same constant for the marker-observed, finalized-marker and two-epoch waits (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:207,211,216) as well as healing. No seconds-per-height catch-up rate is recorded in the result (:204-208). The acceptance page already states a measured live rejoin bound: 'level with the tip within 15 s' (docs/src/spec/testnet-acceptance.md:2006,2062).
rows.consequence: FALSE FAIL on a slow runner (the observed incident) and, if scaled without a cap, FALSE PASS by making the wait long enough to absorb a stall. The bound is not a property of the system, so a red result is not attributable and a green one is not a rate.
rows.current_behaviour: 150 s for healing; on expiry a single RuntimeError (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:141). The same 150 s is also the base drill's deadline for reaching a future epoch boundary (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:207,211,216), so one constant conflates four different waits.
rows.safeguard: Compute W = max(15 s, gap_heights * measured_seconds_per_height * k), where seconds_per_height is measured in the same run from the victim's own last-finalized advance between samples, k is pre-registered (e.g. 3), and W is capped at a pre-registered maximum (e.g. 300 s). Record gap, rate, k, W and the observed pass time in the result. Keep the catch-up target frozen so a large W cannot mask a stall, and fail the run when the rate is missing.
rows.formalizable: Law 71 bounds the catch-up window for the walk (spec/LAWS.md:198), not the harness's deadline; the deadline is a layer. State it as a layer; no law is owed.
rows.falsifier: Throttle the victim's bandwidth (or use a recorded slow run) and show the verdict is unchanged; assert seconds_per_height is present and >0 in the result.

rows.deviation: The healing health gate never reads the node's finality-stall ALARM. It records the per-block diagnostic string and lets a sustained-stalled node count as healthy.
rows.cause: node/src/web/http.rs:1496 documents finalityStalled as 'the field to alarm on' and :1495 documents finalityStall as the per-block diagnosis, explicitly 'NOT an alarm'. The gate records operator.get('finalityStall') (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:50) but its health predicate checks only ready, orphanBodies, pipelineFaults and proposalHalted (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:71-76). finalityStalled and finalityCountersDurable are never read or recorded.
rows.consequence: FALSE PASS: a node whose finality is sustained-stalled, or whose counters are process-local because the store is unreadable (finalityCountersDurable false, node/src/web/http.rs:1498), passes the health gate; its old marker and height may still satisfy the anchor, and the run certifies 'healthy' for a node the operator surface says is stalled. The verdict then misattributes a stall to the rejoin predicate (AG-01) rather than to the node.
rows.current_behaviour: finality_stall is recorded (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:50) but not gated; finalityStalled and finalityStallEpisodes are absent from the status row.
rows.safeguard: Add `finalityStalled is False` and `finalityCountersDurable is True` to the health predicate, failing closed when either is missing; record finalityStallEpisodes and compare it across samples (a monotone counter, so a rise during the healing window is STALLED/DIVERGED rather than 'healthy'). Test with a fixture row where finalityStalled=true and every other field is clean.
rows.formalizable: Law 54a (spec/LAWS.md:84): a liveness predicate must read the current view, not a history. Reading the per-block finalityStall string instead of the current finalityStalled boolean is that error; the gate is a layer over the operator surface.
rows.falsifier: A fixture with finalityStalled=true and all other counters clean must fail the health gate; the current predicate passes it.

rows.deviation: The offline negative controls exercise a MOCKED predicate and skip the live-path gates, so they cannot catch the predicate drift that caused the incident; the failing run is not replayed as a fixture.
rows.cause: tests/test_recovery_harness_controls.py:30-34 builds WorkloadDrill with object.__new__ and replaces finalized_marker with a Mock. The default fixture leaves `events` unset, so getattr(self,'events',None) at tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:37 and :69 disables both the divergence and the health gates in most cases. The tests at :48-69 assert the exact-equality behaviour that IS the defect. The release job runs only this file plus py_compile (.github/workflows/isolated-finality-recovery-16gb.yml:233-235); tests/consensus-drill-regression.py runs only in devnet-fuzz.yml:735.
rows.consequence: FALSE PASS at the harness layer: the gate can be changed to a wrong predicate, or the live ordering (health before marker, divergence before marker) broken, with every control green. The regression that produced run 41208692673 had no offline reproducer; discovery cost a hosted run and manual reading of observations.
rows.current_behaviour: Mocked finalized_marker; health/divergence paths only exercised when a test sets `events`; no test loads the failed trace or asserts a verdict classification.
rows.safeguard: Extract a pure rejoin_verdict(rows, anchor, heals) and table-test it with at minimum: the real failed trace (seven healthy at 67-69, victim monotone 56-63 -> LAGGING, not DIVERGED); a fork at the anchor -> DIVERGED; a victim below the anchor -> LAGGING; a stale anchor; and a same-height conflicting hash -> DIVERGED. Make the default fixture exercise the health/divergence path and assert gate ordering. Add a replay test over a committed, minimized observations.jsonl. Run the drill-regression suite in the release job.
rows.formalizable: Layer (test harness), not a law. The property under test is predicate monotonicity, which is Law 15's (spec/LAWS.md:70).
rows.falsifier: Revert the fixed predicate to exact equality: the new control suite must go red. Feed the failed run's trace: the verdict must be LAGGING and the gate must pass only after the post-reconnect target.
rows.cost: ~1 day.

rows.deviation: The published result upgrades a finite liveness/membership witness into a safety-flavoured 'unanimous finalized height/hash' agreement claim, as well as conflating the N8 isolated drill with criterion 2's live-net witness.
rows.cause: docs/src/spec/testnet-acceptance.md:42-45 says the page is a liveness and membership verdict, not a safety verdict, and that none of the criteria measures whether two validators can finalise conflicting blocks. tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:5-6 says 'finite execution witness, not a universal rollback-safety proof', and tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:206-207 publishes 'retention and finality progression ... not universal CBC safety'. Yet spec/audit/hardfork-51-closeout.md:42 publishes 'unanimous eight-node finalized height/hash after each rejoin'. The drill observes eight local oracles; it does not verify quorum justifications (available on /api/block/{hash} but unused). The live criterion 2 witness is an N3 run (docs/src/spec/testnet-acceptance.md:2006,2062), not this N8 drill.
rows.consequence: FALSE PASS by overclaim: a reader takes an agreement/safety result where only an N=8 finite liveness witness exists. At ad77fb442 the same sentence is false on arm 1 and true on arm 2, so it is not a stable observation either. Downstream plans and the release decision are then justified by a stronger claim than was measured.
rows.current_behaviour: Result string PASS_BOUNDED_WORKLOAD_PARTITION_REJOIN with a prose 'scope' field (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:204-208); the closeout restates it in prose as unanimity.
rows.safeguard: Generate the result string from the asserted predicate list and a fixed verdict vocabulary (e.g. PASS_ANCHOR_AGREEMENT, PASS_PROGRESSION, PASS_RETENTION as separate booleans); forbid 'agree'/'unanimous' unless exact equality was observed on a frozen sample; record the negated claims explicitly ('not checked: universal safety, conflicting finalisation above H*, criterion 2 live rejoin'); make the closeout cite the result file rather than relabel it. Add a schema test that rejects an unknown or overclaiming verdict.
rows.formalizable: The universal safety statement is Law 15/52a territory (spec/LAWS.md:70,79) and is not witnessed by a finite run; the honest treatment is a layer with the law cited as the assumption the witness relies on, not as proved. Owed: the claim vocabulary as checked data.
rows.falsifier: Feed the drill result to the closeout emitter and assert the published sentence is generated from the verdict fields; mutation: hand-write 'unanimous' over a result carrying only anchor agreement and the check must fail.

rows.deviation: The healing gate certifies EXACT equality of every node's current last-finalized (height, hash). That is a synchrony artifact, not criterion 2's witness (survivors finalise past the kill; the rejoiner resumes), and it measures scheduling rather than the property.
rows.cause: Commit 888a0b92c (2026-10-21) deliberately replaced marker retention at a common minimum height with exact identity equality (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:85), polled by the wait at tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:184-185 under tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:122-141. Honest nodes legitimately differ: last_finalized_block_unsafe returns the max member of each node's OWN latest fringe (block-storage/src/dag/representation.rs:77-90), and finalized_blocks_set is the seen-closure (representation.rs:61-67), so two honest nodes on one chain can report different heights. The run's own evidence shows this: the seven online nodes read 67-69 while the victim was 56-63.
rows.consequence: FALSE FAIL. Run 41208692673 arm 1 cycle 2 (ad77fb442) timed out at 150 s with the victim ready, orphanBodies=0, pipelineFaults=0, unrestorableRecords=0 and monotone finality; the same commit's arm 2 passed and 7c24c3b53 failed identically 16 h earlier. Because one binary digest both passes and fails, the gate is not a property of the system at all, and the release decision is driven by which arm is read. It also contradicts criterion 2's stated witness (docs/src/spec/testnet-acceptance.md:63) and A2.2's measured bound, 'level with the tip within 15 s' (docs/src/spec/testnet-acceptance.md:2006).
rows.current_behaviour: Poll every 2 s to a fixed deadline; pass only when len({(height,hash)})==1 across all eight; otherwise raise 'did not pass within 150s' (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:141). The same exact-equality predicate is duplicated in the quiet arm at tests/consensus-quiet-finality.py:45-56 and its rejoin check at :232-234, so a fix local to the partition drill leaves the acceptance package with the defect.
rows.safeguard: R1: delete exact last-finalized equality from the acceptance path and expose one pure, shared, monotone verdict function (the shape already exists at tests/restart_under_load_controls.py:9-20, and tests/consensus-restart-under-load.py:119-141 already rejects same-height hash conflicts while sampling, which is the right monotone safety check). Accept only predicates monotone in each node's finalized set: all-8 is-finalized(anchor) (Law 15) plus a catch-up target frozen once at healing start. On timeout record the best-common-finalized block, per-node lag, and a verdict enum {LAGGING, DIVERGED, STALLED, CONFIG}, and assert the classification in a test. No temporal tolerance is used for the equality claim because the claim is removed; head movement can no longer defeat a correct run.
rows.formalizable: Law 15 (Rchain.seen_monotone_of_reaches, spec/LAWS.md:70) makes 'is-finalized' membership monotone; Law 71 (Rchain.Sync.windowPending_independent_of_tip, spec/LAWS.md:198) is the same 'progress must not depend on the tip standing still' statement for the catch-up walk. Last-finalized-head equality is not a law; the observed 67/69 spread among seven healthy nodes is its refutation. Owed candidate law: 'A rejoin acceptance predicate is sound only if it is monotone in each participant's finalized set; equality of current last-finalized heads is not.' Witness: run 41208692673.
rows.falsifier: Replay the failed arm's observations.jsonl (or a minimized trace of seven healthy nodes at 67-69 that share an ancestor): the current predicate must time out and the fixed predicate must pass. Then mutate the fixed predicate back to exact equality and the new control must go red.
rows.cost: ~1 day: rewrite the condition, extract the shared verdict function, table tests; no node changes.

rows.node: Acceptance governance — repetition and retry policy
rows.deviation: The acceptance verdict is per-arm and never aggregated. The same binary digest can both pass and fail, and a green arm can be quoted as 'the campaign passed' — a pass where the evidence contains a fail.
rows.cause: .github/workflows/isolated-finality-recovery-16gb.yml:193-195 runs matrix repetitions [1,2] with fail-fast:false; each job's exit code is independent (:274-278). The closeout cites a single commit's pass (spec/audit/hardfork-51-closeout.md:42). Nothing in the repo defines k-of-n or forbids citing a subset. The observed evidence is the exact contradiction: ad77fb442 arm 1 failed while arm 2 passed, and 7c24c3b53 failed identically 16 h earlier.
rows.consequence: FALSE PASS if a green arm is quoted, FALSE FAIL if a red arm blocks; retrying until green converts a sampling artifact into evidence. Acceptance becomes unfalsifiable because there is always a passing sample, and the release decision is made on one arm's luck.
rows.current_behaviour: Two independent jobs; the workflow is red if any job is red; no aggregate record; artifacts are named per repetition (isolated-finality-recovery-16gb.yml:354).
rows.safeguard: Define acceptance over all repetitions at one source_sha and one binary_sha256: PASS iff every arm passes, with per-arm results and the aggregate in one checked record. Add a conflict rule: if the same (gate_id, source_sha, binary_sha256) has both PASS and FAIL, mark the GATE INVALID and block acceptance until the predicate is fixed — do not retry. Publish the aggregate, never a subset.
rows.formalizable: A layer (no theorem); the determinism assumption behind 'same binary, same property' is not proved. Law 15/71 underpin the gate but not the repetition policy.
rows.falsifier: A repository check that scans acceptance evidence for one (source_sha, binary_sha256, gate_id) and fails on a PASS/FAIL conflict; offline, feed two contradictory result files and see the aggregator refuse.
rows.cost: ~1 day.

rows.deviation: The acceptance is a PROSE claim: no checker binds a pass to an artifact, predicate version, source digest or binary digest, and the artifact can be lost without failing the run. The pass is published before it can be independently reproduced.
rows.cause: spec/audit/hardfork-51-closeout.md:42 asserts the N8 campaign passed on 69bf868f with 'unanimous eight-node finalized height/hash'. tools/check-hardfork-51-closeout.py:80-166 validates only ledger ids, URLs, owners and git ancestry (:118-120); it never reads a drill result. The workflow's verdict is the trial process exit code (.github/workflows/isolated-finality-recovery-16gb.yml:274-278) and the evidence upload is if-no-files-found: warn (:350-357). The in-tree result has source_sha but no binary digest (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:204-208); only observations.jsonl records a binary digest (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:170-174). The pinned pass itself used the racy predicate: git show 69bf868f:tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:29.
rows.consequence: FALSE PASS at the governance layer. The closeout can state a pass no repository check can reproduce or refute; after GitHub's 90-day artifact retention the claim is unfalsifiable. A broken upload leaves the job green. The accepted 69bf868f pass is a sample from the gate that now fails on ad77fb442, so 'passed' records a lucky run, not a property.
rows.current_behaviour: TRACKER_MUST_REMAIN_OPEN is computed from the authored ledger, with limitations text (tools/check-hardfork-51-closeout.py:157-166) but no acceptance-artifact validation; evidence lives only in a GitHub artifact with 90-day retention (isolated-finality-recovery-16gb.yml:357).
rows.safeguard: Introduce a machine-readable acceptance record with required fields: gate_id, gate_version/predicate digest, source_dev_sha, binary_sha256, run_id, artifact_sha256, per-arm result, window, anchor, and measurements. Extend check-hardfork-51-closeout.py to require that record for each acceptance row and to compare its digests with the cited commit. Archive the result JSON under spec/audit/evidence/<run>/ with its digest (the pattern of spec/audit/evidence/hardfork-51-integrated-20261021.md) and change the upload to if-no-files-found: error. Bound: the judge re-reads the artifact digest, not the prose.
rows.formalizable: A layer/process invariant, not a Lean law: 'a published pass names an artifact whose digest matches and whose source/binary digest matches the cited commit'. Owed checker rule; no theorem is claimed.
rows.falsifier: Remove or alter one field of the result JSON and show the checker refuses closeout; run check-hardfork-51-closeout.py against a ledger whose acceptance row has no artifact and require a non-zero exit.
rows.cost: ~1 day schema + checker + one archived run.

rows.deviation: A failed campaign leaves two contradictory verdict files in the same directory: `result.json` still says `"result": "pass"` (the workload half) while `partition-result.json` says `FAIL_BOUNDED_WORKLOAD_PARTITION_REJOIN`. The base drill's pass summary is written before any partition phase and is never invalidated when the campaign fails.
rows.cause: tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:136 calls `d.run()` directly, so tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:219-223 writes `result.json` = pass into the same `out` (`Drill.__init__` tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:73-75); the failure writer `record_cycle` (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:101-125) writes `partition-result.json` (FAIL) but does not touch `result.json`; the fail-writing branch of the base drill, tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:238-242 (inside `a.main()`), is bypassed because `a.main()` is never called.
rows.consequence: False PASS for any consumer that treats `result.json` as the campaign verdict — and there is one in-tree: tests/consensus-post-restart-proposal.py:108-110 reads `out/result.json` and `out/observations.jsonl` from the very same directory (workflow invokes both with `--out target/isolated-16gb/n8-partition`, isolated-finality-recovery-16gb.yml:274 and :311). An auditor grepping the artifact for `"result": "pass"` finds a pass in a red run.
rows.current_behaviour: Two verdicts coexist; the campaign's FAIL is authoritative only if the reader knows the filename convention.
rows.safeguard: Make the ambiguity unrepresentable: rename the base drill's artifact to `workload-result.json` and let the campaign write the only `result.json`; on a failed cycle, delete or overwrite any `result.json` whose result is pass. Add an assertion in the campaign writer that its result equals the worst cycle result. Bound: no file named `result.json` may ever contain a result weaker than the campaign's.
rows.formalizable: Layer of protection only; this is an evidence-addressing defect, not a consensus property.
rows.falsifier: Unit test: pre-populate a temp dir with `Drill.run`'s output, drive a failing cycle through `record_cycle`, assert no file parsed from `result.json` reports pass (today the test fails).
rows.cost: A rename plus a two-line assertion; one test.

rows.deviation: Every distinct failure of the healing gate is signalled late, at the deadline, as one generic message. `wait()` raises `'... did not pass within 150s; last read error=None'` (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:141) for at least seven different predicates: unhealthy node, unrestorable-records divergence, any node below `min_height`, marker lost or changed, wrong node set, unequal (height,hash), and — after the fix — anchor not finalized. `finalized_marker_agreement` returns `None` for each with no reason. The incident's cause (victim lagging while every node had finalized the anchor) is indistinguishable in the artifact from a genuine hash fork.
rows.cause: tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:29-87 returns `None` at :58, :77, :81, :84 and :86 without naming the clause; tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:122-141 records only read/drive errors and discards the last successful observation when the deadline fires; the timeout RuntimeError at :141 carries no per-node state.
rows.consequence: False FAIL (a correct system is rejected and the run cannot be triaged) and operational debt: the incident needed a human to reconstruct 150 s of jsonl to prove the victim was healthy and lagging rather than forked. A fork and a lag produce the same artifact.
rows.current_behaviour: One untyped timeout string; the last poll's identities are recorded only if the equality branch reached the marker read.
rows.safeguard: Introduce a typed reason: `{LAG, FORK_AT_ANCHOR, MARKER_LOST, UNHEALTHY, DIVERGED, SET_MISMATCH, BELOW_TARGET}`, returned (or raised as a typed error) by the gate, recorded as `verdict_reason` on every poll and at timeout together with the offending node, its height, its hash and its raw `is-finalized` answer. The timeout message names the clause and the node. Note the required asymmetry: a false `is-finalized` among the seven online nodes at healing start fails immediately (R2), while a false among all eight after reconnect is a bounded wait, not an immediate failure — encoding the first rule for all eight would make the arm a false-FAIL machine.
rows.formalizable: Law 51 is literally this taxonomy: shapes `Void`/`Terminal`/`Drift` and causes `Historic`/`ReadsTheView`/`Split` (spec/Rchain/Progress.lean; spec/INVENTORY.md:190). A victim slower than its peers is a pacing/history problem; two finalized-but-different anchors is `Split`. The drill should emit the vocabulary the model already has.
rows.falsifier: A test feeding the incident shape (victim below target, all seven online true for B*, victim eventually true) asserts `verdict_reason == "LAG"` and PASS; a test feeding two different hashes at the anchor asserts `FORK_AT_ANCHOR` and FAIL.
rows.cost: A small enum, one classifier callback, one field per poll; two tests.

rows.deviation: The PASS artifact records neither the bound it passed under nor — under the proposed fix — the one object every node is claimed to share. `partition-result.json` (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:204-208) has no `window`, no `H*`/`B*`, no per-node `is-finalized` answers. Today an exact-equality PASS implies a common (height,hash); the proposed anchor fix deliberately allows heads to differ, so unless B* and the eight answers are written, the PASS artifact contains no common finalized block at all. Additionally `finalized_marker` returns `None` at tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:150-151 before recording a node below `min_height`, so a lagging-victim poll stores only the online nodes' identities.
rows.cause: tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:131 hard-codes `args.window=150` and never records it; :186 stores `rejoined` (identities) only; tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:143-159 records per-node reads but the timeout path (:141) keeps only `last_error`; the equality predicate at tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:80-87 is the only thing that implies a shared block, and the fix removes it.
rows.consequence: False PASS: a PASS whose witness does not include the anchor. An auditor cannot re-derive H*, B*, that the seven online nodes agreed on B* at healing start, or that all eight finalized it — the exact facts the fix is supposed to establish. If a scaled window is adopted, the PASS is additionally bounded by an unstated number, so two arms are incomparable.
rows.current_behaviour: The verdict is a list of per-node heads plus the bare word FAIL/PASS; the endpoint `/api/is-finalized` (node/src/web/http.rs:2088) is never read, so the anchor is not even observed today.
rows.safeguard: The verdict gains a single `anchor` object written on PASS and on FAIL: `{"height": H*, "hash": B*, "online_finality": [7 answers at healing start], "rejoined_finality": [8 answers at PASS], "window_seconds": w, "victim_gap_at_rejoin": g}`. The PASS writer asserts all eight `rejoined_finality` are exactly `True` and that `w` is present. Bound the window by measurement, not a guess: `w = max(150, k * g)` with `k` stated (suggest k=4, four median block intervals per block of gap) and `g` measured at reconnect and recorded. With this record the proposed fix is sound; without it the fix trades a non-monotone predicate for an unwitnessed one.
rows.formalizable: The underlying property is law 14's finality gate (spec/INVENTORY.md:88) and law 58's forward dual; law 71's monotone frontier (`run_monotone`, spec/INVENTORY.md:210) explains why a fixed anchor, not a moving head, is the correct predicate. Recording the anchor is a layer, not a law; the measured `k` is a decision, not a theorem.
rows.falsifier: Success-path control asserts `partition-result.json["rounds"][i]["anchor"]["rejoined_finality"] == [true]*8` and that `window_seconds` is present; deleting the anchor from the writer makes the control red.
rows.cost: Eight extra GETs at two instants, one field, one control test.

rows.deviation: Causal capture is hard-bounded at height 256 and its refusal never affects the verdict. `capture()` raises `'capture height outside bounded 0..256 range'` for any node whose `latestBlockNumber > 256`, records a per-node error and `complete_capture: false`, and the drill still writes PASS. A campaign with two 300 s online-progress cycles at ~5 s per deploy can cross 256; when it does, every node's capture is refused and the PASS artifact has no DAG at all.

rows.node: HC — the healing checker: anchor selection, is-finalized predicate, health/divergence gates, window, verdicts
rows.deviation: With heads allowed to differ, the marker read is performed AS WELL AS the anchor read but adds no agreement: finalized_marker probes the marker at each node's own last-finalized block, proving each node is self-consistent, not that the nodes agree. A node on a diverging branch above B* carries the pre-partition marker and passes.
rows.cause: finalized_marker reads snapshot() and probes probe(i, self.marker, block_hash) using that node's own hash (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:143-159, called at tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:80). The marker was deployed and finalized before the partition, so it is present in any pre-partition state. The proposal explicitly drops head equality ('Heads may differ'), leaving the single boolean is_finalized(B*) at one height as the only cross-node state comparison; nothing above B* is compared.
rows.consequence: False PASS: a victim or online node that finalized B* and then follows a divergent branch above it passes the healing verdict. The equality check was wrong (HC-OTHER-1, HC-PART-1) but it was the only cross-node comparison, so the proposal removes the defect and its only agreement evidence together.
rows.current_behaviour: Marker evidence is per-node and recorded per-node; `rejoined` therefore proves retention, not agreement.
rows.safeguard: Probe the marker at the fixed anchor on every node: probe(i, marker, B*) for all eight, requiring the marker value in B*'s post-state. That is a cross-node state commitment at a fixed point with no representative involved and is monotone in the seen set exactly as is_finalized(B*) is. Additionally require each of the seven online nodes to answer is_finalized of every other online node's own representative (O(49) probes, trivial for a drill) so a divergence above B* is detected instead of only at B*.
rows.formalizable: Law 14b gives one message per bonded sender in the fringe, but the state identity at a fixed block is only assumed by deterministic replay. Owed: post_state_is_a_function_of_block — two nodes replaying the same accepted block B produce the same explore-deploy answer for a marker written before B; falsified by any node whose state at B differs. Until then this is a layer of protection.
rows.falsifier: Offline control: node 7 answers is_finalized(B*) true and retains the marker at its own head but reports a different block at B*+1; the marker-at-B* probe returns empty — must FAIL. HEAD passes it.
rows.cost: ~10 lines, reusing probe; 8 extra state reads per poll.

rows.node: HC — the healing checker: anchor selection, is-finalized predicate, health/divergence gates, window, verdicts
rows.deviation: The verdict can be issued EARLY: it is the first satisfying sample of a non-monotone conjunction, with no post-rejoin progress requirement and no stability window, so a victim that answers from pre-partition state and ingests nothing is admitted.
rows.cause: wait returns on the first non-None condition (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:125-130) and finalized_marker_agreement is one pass over a conjunction of gauges — ready, orphanBodies, pipelineFaults, proposalHalted (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:69-77) — then finalized_marker(min_height, required=True) (line 80). finalityStall is recorded but never gated (line 50); the alarm field finalityStalled is published by both surfaces (node/src/api/dto.rs:282; node/src/web/http.rs:766,1496-1498) and never read; peers is recorded (line 49) and never gated. The anchor's non-vacuity is assumed, not measured: `before` is node 0's height only (line 154) and the victim's pre-partition finalized height is never sampled, so H* = min over the online seven can be <= the victim's stale height and is_finalized(B*) is already true at the first poll.
rows.consequence: False PASS: a stalled victim, or one whose L2 reconnect succeeded while its peer connections did not (peers=0), passes whenever B* is already in its seen set. The evidence cannot distinguish that from a real rejoin because the victim's before and after heights are not both recorded.
rows.current_behaviour: Single-sample conjunction; no K-of-K stability; no progress predicate; no peers or finalityStalled gate; drive=False (line 27) means no workload is supplied during healing, so progress cannot be inferred from deploys either.
rows.safeguard: Require (a) K consecutive satisfying samples (e.g. 3 x 2 s) so a transient gauge cannot satisfy the conjunction; (b) the victim's own finalized height strictly greater than its recorded pre-partition height AND >= H*, with before/after written to partition-result.json; (c) finalityStalled == false and finalityStallEpisodes unchanged from the pre-partition snapshot; (d) peers >= the victim's pre-partition peer count (or a documented floor). Bound K by the same measured window as HC-LESS-1.
rows.formalizable: Law 58's forward dual (the gate publishes on a fully-participating set, spec/LAWS.md:88) is the relevant law, but its schedule hypothesis — a fully-live set reaches a full partition within N rounds — is named and unproved. The harness's progress predicate is a finite witness of that hypothesis, not a theorem. Layer plus owed witness: after rejoin the victim's last-finalized height strictly increases and reaches H*; falsified by a victim that answers true and stays at H*.
rows.falsifier: Live negative arm: reconnect the victim's network but block block delivery (or kill its peer connections) and assert the healing verdict FAILS; today it passes when H* <= victim_pre. Offline: a control where the anchor is at or below the victim's pre-partition height and no progress occurs must FAIL.
rows.cost: ~25 lines, one extra recorded pre-partition sample, one live negative arm.

rows.node: HC — the healing checker: anchor selection, is-finalized predicate, health/divergence gates, window, verdicts
rows.deviation: The verdict is issued LATER than the bound it claims: the deadline is tested only at the top of the poll loop, and one condition evaluation can run for minutes past it while the error text still says 'within 150s'.
rows.cause: tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:122-141 tests deadline at the loop top, then runs condition() unbounded, then sleeps 2 s. One evaluation of finalized_marker_agreement is 8 operator + 8 health + 8 last-finalized + 8 probes = 32 requests (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:37-55,80; tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:84-94,143-159), 40 with the proposed is-finalized read; every get has timeout=10 (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:35). A poll starting 1 s before the deadline can therefore run ~320-400 s. The elapsed time is never recorded and the failure message hard-codes args.window (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:141).
rows.consequence: The verdict overstates its own evidence: a repair completing at 400 s can be reported as 'did not pass within 150s' (false FAIL on the property) or, if it had passed during the overrun, as passing a bound it exceeded (false PASS on the bound). The same arithmetic inflates the 300 s online window at tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:158-161.
rows.current_behaviour: No per-poll time budget, no elapsed field, no min(10, remaining) clamping; the only control patches monotonic to [0,0,151] (tests/test_recovery_harness_controls.py:142-150), which cannot see an overrun.
rows.safeguard: Pass the deadline into the reader and use timeout=min(10, remaining); record elapsed_sec and polls in the healing record and in partition-result.json; assert elapsed <= window + one poll in the control. State the bound as 'the last poll starts before the deadline', which is what the code actually enforces.
rows.formalizable: No node theorem — this is harness arithmetic. Layer: an operational tolerance that must be recorded as measured (companion to HC-LESS-1).
rows.falsifier: A control whose condition sleeps 60 s with a 10 s window must raise within window + one poll and report elapsed > window; HEAD's control cannot distinguish this from the mocked case.
rows.cost: ~8 lines plus elapsed recording.

rows.node: HC — the healing checker: anchor selection, is-finalized predicate, health/divergence gates, window, verdicts
rows.deviation: The 150 s healing window is LESS than the node's own ordinary block-request maintenance time constant, and it is not derived from any measurement of the victim's finalized gap or catch-up rate.
rows.cause: tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:131 hard-codes args.window=150, consumed by deadline = monotonic() + window (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:122-124). The retriever's default request age is 240 s (requested_blocks_timeout: secs(240), node/src/configuration/configuration.rs:872); the 30 s renewal lease is a newer, narrower path (casper/src/blocks/block_retriever.rs:25-28). The drill's own evidence records a run where 'the 150-second healing wait ended before ordinary 240-second request maintenance retried them' (tests/evidence/n8-broadcast-handoff-20261021.md:73), and another where a healthy online group advanced 56->59 and the healing condition still failed the separate 150 s bound (spec/audit/evidence/hardfork-51-integrated-20261021.md:10).
rows.consequence: False FAIL of a healthy victim whose missing ancestor sits on the maintenance path. The 150 s number is not a bound the recovery mechanism promises, so the drill rejects correct systems for being slower than an unmeasured constant. With the anchor fix (HC-OTHER-1) this becomes the next failure mode, not an eliminated one.
rows.current_behaviour: Hard 150 s for both cycles; the victim is never sampled before the partition (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:154 samples node 0 only), so neither its gap nor its rate is available to justify or scale the bound.
rows.safeguard: Record the victim's pre-partition (height,hash); at rejoin compute gap g = H* - victim_height and measure catch-up over the first two polls; set the healing bound to max(240 s floor, k * g / rate) with k pre-registered (e.g. 3) and record g, rate and the derived bound in partition-result.json. Alternatively use a monotone-progress predicate (the victim's finalized height strictly increases every poll and reaches H*) with a large ceiling instead of a tight wall clock. The floor is a tolerance and must be stated: 240 s is the retriever's own maintenance constant, not a measurement of this net.
rows.formalizable: Law 58's 3 x LIVENESS_WINDOW factor is explicitly 'measured, not proved' (spec/LAWS.md:88) — this row is the same class of operational tolerance, so it must be recorded as a measurement rather than asserted as a law. Declare it a layer.
rows.falsifier: A run whose gap/rate exceeds 150 s (or the in-tree 240 s evidence reproduced) must PASS under the scaled bound and FAIL under the fixed one; the control must also assert elapsed_sec <= window.
rows.cost: ~20 lines and one extra recorded sample; no node change.

rows.node: HC — the healing checker: anchor selection, is-finalized predicate, health/divergence gates, window, verdicts
rows.deviation: The health gate demands MORE than a healthy node can give: pipelineFaults must be exactly 0 on all eight nodes, but pipelineFaults is a process-wide cumulative counter with no reset, so one historical fault permanently makes the healing condition unsatisfiable and is reported as a healing timeout.
rows.cause: The gate is `x['pipeline_faults'] != 0 ... -> return None` (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:69-77). The counter is `static PIPELINE_FAULTS: AtomicU64` incremented by fetch_add(1) (casper/src/blocks/block_processor.rs:33,36-48), with no store anywhere in the workspace (a workspace-wide grep for PIPELINE_FAULTS returns exactly those three sites). It is incremented on received-block faults (casper/src/blocks/block_processor.rs:129,174; casper/src/blocks/block_receiver.rs:587) — precisely the events a partition/rejoin under load produces. /health folds it into `blocked` and hence `ready` (node/src/web/http.rs:735-746), so after one fault ready=false and pipelineFaults>0 persist for the process lifetime, failing both halves of the gate forever.
rows.consequence: Permanent false FAIL. A fault during the 300 s online phase poisons the healing gate for both cycles, and the verdict names neither the counter nor its pre-existing value. The orphanBodies half is a clearing gauge (casper/src/block_disposition.rs:1325-1350) and is defensible; the pipelineFaults half is not.
rows.current_behaviour: The offline control tests orphanBodies=26 but never a pre-existing nonzero pipelineFaults (tests/test_recovery_harness_controls.py:82-89); a live run with one fault gets a generic healing timeout.
rows.safeguard: Snapshot pipelineFaults and orphanBodies at healing start and gate on the delta after reconnect: zero NEW faults during healing (stated bound), while a pre-existing nonzero is recorded and emitted as PIPELINE_FAULT_PREEXISTING — a distinct verdict, not a liveness timeout. Apply the same delta rule to unres torableRecords while keeping the absolute >0 permanent-divergence check, and read finalityCountersDurable (node/src/api/dto.rs:290-299) so a non-durable zero is not accepted as proof of none.
rows.formalizable: Law 54 clause a (spec/INVENTORY.md:193): a liveness predicate must read the current view; a rule over a retention/history counter is Historic. pipelineFaults is a history and the checker uses it as a current-state predicate — the same class the law names, and currentOf_iff is the theorem that says the two readings are not interchangeable.
rows.falsifier: Offline control: health reports pipelineFaults=1 at healing start and the same value afterwards with everything else healthy — must PASS (HEAD returns None forever). Live: inject one fault in the online phase and assert the healing verdict is PIPELINE_FAULT_PREEXISTING.
rows.cost: ~10 lines, one control; no node change (the node's own permanent ready=false is a separate, node-side finding).

rows.node: HC — the healing checker: anchor selection, is-finalized predicate, health/divergence gates, window, verdicts
rows.deviation: The proposal's claim that 'a fork among the seven fails immediately' does NOT hold, and the check cannot separate an online node that is merely lagging from one that has refuted B*; both consume the whole window and emit the same liveness timeout. The predicate also fails to distinguish an empty/absent fringe from a false answer.
rows.cause: Every negative answer inside a condition is `return None` and wait retries (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:122-141); the only immediate verdicts are the marker-lost RuntimeError (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:154-157) and PERMANENT_DIVERGENCE (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:59-65). is_finalized is local DAG membership (block-storage/src/dag/representation.rs:141-143), so a node that has not yet ingested B* answers a well-formed `false`, not an error; and a node with no fringe answers `false` too, because finalized_blocks_set() is empty (block-storage/src/dag/representation.rs:62-68) whereas last-finalized-block is a 400 'Finalized fringe is not available.' (block-storage/src/dag/representation.rs:87-91; casper/src/api/block_api_impl.rs:1113-1125; node/src/web/http.rs:925-927, 355-360). finalized_marker swallows that 400 as `return None` even under required=True (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:145-149).
rows.consequence: False FAIL plus verdict confusion: a benign lag, a real divergence among the online seven, a victim that never reconnects, and a node that has permanently lost its fringe all produce 'healing did not pass within 150s'. The review's question whether verdicts distinguish safety from liveness is answered no, except for PERMANENT_DIVERGENCE.
rows.current_behaviour: One result string FAIL_BOUNDED_WORKLOAD_PARTITION_REJOIN with failed_phase (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:115-120); the anchor answer and the per-node online verdicts are not recorded at all.
rows.safeguard: Sample the seven once at healing start and require unanimity on is_finalized(B*) within a short measured bound (e.g. 3 polls x 2 s, or one retriever maintenance lease) before raising a distinct ONLINE_STALE / ONLINE_DIVERGENCE verdict naming the node and its answer; require the victim's answers separately. Under required=True, treat the empty-fringe 400 as a loud verdict, not as 'still catching up'. Bounded retry is required because B* may be published-but-not-yet-ingested by an online node; 'immediately' would itself be a false FAIL.
rows.formalizable: Law 52 clause a / Law 14a for the underlying finality agreement; the observation-side bound is a harness property with no node theorem. Owed: observation_agrees_after_delivery — a block published by a supermajority is answered true by every node once delivery completes, and a false answer after the bound is a safety violation. Witness: two nodes, one fixed finalized block, delivery complete -> both true; force one to answer false -> violation. Until the law exists this row is a layer of protection, not a law.
rows.falsifier: Two offline controls: (a) one of the seven always answers false, the rest true — must raise ONLINE_DIVERGENCE, not the generic timeout; (b) one answers false for one poll then true — must pass. HEAD produces the same timeout for both.
rows.cost: ~30 lines plus two controls; no node change.

rows.node: HC — the healing checker: anchor selection, is-finalized predicate, health/divergence gates, window, verdicts
rows.deviation: The healing verdict measures something other than the property: it requires exact equality of (finalized height, hash) across all eight nodes at one sample of a chain on which the seven online nodes are still finalizing and do not agree with each other.
rows.cause: tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:80-86 returns only when len({(height,hash)}) == 1 over all 8 identities; tests/test_recovery_harness_controls.py:48-51 codifies 'different heights is not agreement'. But drive=False (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:21-27) suppresses only helper deploys, not autopropose or finality: the recorded run has the seven online nodes at 67/68/69 at the end while the anchor was 48, and their last-finalized blocks differ by height because each is at a different point of the same advancing fringe (`last_finalized_block_hash` = max (height,id) over `latest_fringe()`, block-storage/src/dag/representation.rs:77-82). The conjunction therefore demands a sample in which eight nodes at different heights report equal (height,hash); on a producing chain none exists and the wait can only reach its deadline.
rows.consequence: False FAIL of a healthy, converging victim — and of the online set itself. Run 41208692673, N8 arm 1 cycle 2, is an instance: victim healthy, anchor (48) passed at ~+66 s, wait timed out at 150 s. The verdict is uncorrelated with the property it claims to test, so a safety regression could also be hidden behind the same timeout (see HC-NO-1).
rows.current_behaviour: Polls every 2 s for args.window seconds (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:122-141) and raises one generic RuntimeError at the deadline; the equality is recomputed from scratch each poll and no per-node retention or progress is carried across polls.
rows.safeguard: Replace the head equality with a fixed finalized anchor taken from the pre-reconnect sample (`identities`, tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:167-172, whose last value is used at :183): H* = min finalized height over the seven online nodes, B* = its hash; require each of the seven to answer GET /api/is-finalized/{B*} true (bounded retry, see HC-NO-1); after reconnect require all eight true, plus the existing health/divergence gates and finalized_marker(H*, required=True). Heads may differ; the anchor must come from the pre-connect sample so a read taken while the nodes are healing cannot move it. Record H*, B* and every answer. This deletes the moving-head comparison, leaving only the monotone membership predicate.
rows.formalizable: Law 15 (spec/LAWS.md:70): the seen set is monotone (Rchain.seen_monotone_of_reaches, Rchain.seen_subset_of_mem_seen), so membership of a fixed block in a node's finalized set is the monotone predicate; equality of two nodes' representatives is not a theorem of Law 15, and Rchain.fringe_monotone_is_false proves the fringe side has no such property.
rows.falsifier: A producing 8-node chain with heads 67/68/69 must PASS the anchor predicate within one poll. Invert the offline control test_marker_retention_at_different_heights_is_not_agreement (tests/test_recovery_harness_controls.py:48-51) to assert PASS; it fails under HEAD.

rows.node: HC — the healing checker: anchor selection, is-finalized predicate, health/divergence gates, window, verdicts
rows.deviation: Even with static heads the equality compares only PART OF the evidence: the representative of the finalized set (`max(height,id)` over the latest fringe), not the finalized set. A correct node may change that representative at the same height without losing finality.
rows.cause: block-storage/src/dag/representation.rs:77-82 defines last_finalized_block_hash as max over latest_fringe() of (height,id); latest_fringe() is max_by_key(fringe_height) over the justifications' recorded fringes (block-storage/src/dag/message_map.rs:70-84; block-storage/src/dag/message_state.rs:437-440). Law 15 proves the fringe is not monotone as a set (Rchain.fringe_monotone_is_false, Rchain.cross_sender_height_monotone_is_false, spec/LAWS.md:70) while the seen set is. Two nodes, or one node across two polls, can therefore report the same height with different hashes with no finality lost — and the drill treats that as non-agreement.
rows.consequence: False FAIL. The sibling quiet-finality drill already names and fixes exactly this: tests/consensus-quiet-finality.py:107-119 records the prior (height,hash) and, when the hash changes, requires `/api/is-finalized/{old hash}` to remain true, with the comment 'A growing fringe can change that representative at the same height without losing finality'. The partition drill never adopted the idiom, so an in-tree, already-proved-correct predicate co-exists with the defective one.
rows.current_behaviour: Exact set-cardinality-one on (height,hash); tests/test_recovery_harness_controls.py:53-56 asserts that equal heights with different hashes are not agreement, encoding the defect as expected behaviour.
rows.safeguard: Reuse the quiet-drill predicate on every poll: for each node, if its representative changes, require the previous representative to still answer is_finalized true; never compare representatives across nodes. Cross-node agreement is expressed only as is_finalized(B*) true on a fixed B*.
rows.formalizable: Law 15, the fringe half: Rchain.fringe_monotone_is_false and Rchain.cross_sender_height_monotone_is_false (spec/LAWS.md:70), with the cross-sender counterexample (prev = {m3@3} against published {q2@2}) as the witness that representatives may differ at the same height.
rows.falsifier: Two samples with equal height and different hashes where is-finalized(old) is true must PASS; the control at tests/test_recovery_harness_controls.py:53-56 must be inverted and fails under HEAD.
rows.cost: ~15 lines; the predicate already exists in tests/consensus-quiet-finality.py:107-119.

rows.deviation: `orphanBodies` is a confirmed count whose confirmation latency (3 consecutive 60s samples = 180s) exceeds the 150s healing window, so a runtime orphan created when the victim rejoins is invisible for the entire gate.
rows.cause: `ORPHAN_AUDIT_INTERVAL = 60s` and `ORPHAN_AUDIT_SAMPLES = 3` (casper/src/block_disposition.rs:1313,1320); the audit writes `ORPHAN_BODIES` only on the third consecutive sample (OrphanStreak::observe, :1359-1378; audit loop :1415-1425), while the boot path is immediate (:1331-1340) -> `orphan_bodies()` reads that cell (:1344-1346) -> /health exposes it (node/src/web/http.rs:757) -> the gate requires it ==0 inside `args.window = 150` (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:45,72,131) -> 180s > 150s, so a fresh runtime orphan cannot be observed. The gate also never reads `orphanDetections`, the monotone episode count (:1355-1357).
rows.consequence: False PASS: a victim that rejoins and writes an unaccounted body passes the health gate for the whole window. Secondary: an orphan episode that began and resolved during the cycle reads 0 again and leaves only `orphanDetections`, which the gate ignores, so 'had an orphan' and 'never had one' are indistinguishable.
rows.current_behaviour: orphanBodies==0 is treated as proof of no orphan; it is actually proof of 'none confirmed yet', with a 180s floor.
rows.safeguard: Either (a) require `window >= ORPHAN_AUDIT_SAMPLES * ORPHAN_AUDIT_INTERVAL + probe latency` (>= 200s) and state that bound as measured rather than the current round 150; or (b) record `orphanDetections` at healing start and require it unchanged at the passing sample, which detects an episode without waiting for confirmation. Option (b) is the cheaper and bounded one.
rows.formalizable: Law 88a covers eventual visibility only (`Rchain.Disposition.audit_covers`, `audit_makes_an_unbacked_body_visible`) and states no sampling latency; the gate relies on a property the law does not give. Owed derived bound, not a new law.
rows.falsifier: Inject a store/DAG gap at healing start (a stored body with no DAG entry) and show the current gate passes within 150s; then show the `orphanDetections`-delta check fails at the next audit tick (or the window rule refuses to run at 150s).
rows.cost: One integer read plus a stored baseline, or +50s of window.

rows.node: Readiness and health signals — `pipelineFaults` and `proposalHalted` across a process restart
rows.deviation: After a restart, `pipelineFaults` and `proposalHalted` are fresh zeros because they are process cells with no boot seeding, while the durable fault ledger survives. The health gate of the restart drill is therefore near-vacuous on its first read, and the same applies after a mid-cycle crash in the partition arm.
rows.cause: `PIPELINE_FAULTS` is a static AtomicU64 with exactly three references — declaration, load, increment (casper/src/blocks/block_processor.rs:33-51); the code's own doc says the ledger survives a restart and the cell is what /health reads now (:103-108). `PROPOSAL_ISOLATED` is the same shape (casper/src/blocks/proposer/proposer.rs:944-951) and is cleared only by a restart or admin resume (:955). The restart drill SIGKILLs and restarts the container (tests/consensus-post-restart-proposal.py:152-163) and then requires `pipelineFaults == 0` and `proposalHalted is False` (:64-72) — both are true by construction after a fresh process, even if the durable ledger holds a quarantined block (casper/src/block_disposition.rs:428, `MAX_FAULT_RETRIES = 8` at :128).
rows.consequence: False PASS: a node that faulted or quarantined a block before the restart reports ready and passes the post-restart health gate; the pre-restart fault is invisible on /health. Unrestorable records are persisted, so the two counters disagree in provenance and only the weaker one is read.
rows.current_behaviour: The health gate reports a clean pipeline after every restart even when the durable ledger says otherwise.
rows.safeguard: Node-side R2, the F-U10-02 pattern: publish a durable fault/halt record with a `durable:false` reading when the store cannot be read, or a process-start identity on the status surface. Harness-side: read the boot identity before and after the cycle and refuse to treat a process-scoped counter as evidence when it changed within the window.
rows.formalizable: No Lean law. The worked precedent is F-U10-02, which closed exactly this 'false on a node that never halted vs false on one that halted and restarted' ambiguity for the autopropose timer with `autoproposeHalt {at,durable}` (docs/src/spec/failure-hazop.md:318). The same durable shape is owed for the pipeline fault and proposal isolation.
rows.falsifier: A restart drill where the victim faults a block (forced Internal / missing justification) before the SIGKILL: the current gate passes after `docker start`; the durable-flag or start-stamp version fails.
rows.cost: One durable record and one status field in node code, plus one test; a harness start-stamp if done cheaply first.

rows.node: Readiness and health signals — `ready` as a health/safety proxy
rows.deviation: `ready` means 'can this node include work now' (a liveness/inclusion predicate), and the gate consumes it as a health proxy. A node that stays in NodeRunning while refusing an unrestorable block and all its descendants reports ready=true.
rows.cause: `blocked = !all_running || pipeline_faults > 0 || proposal_isolated || orphan_bodies > 0` and `ready = !blocked` (node/src/web/http.rs:746,752); the module doc states readiness answers 'can this node include work now?' and is not a pressure or safety verdict (:719-732). There is no finality term and no divergence term. The permanent-divergence state is documented as staying in NodeRunning and continuing to serve (spec/AUDIT.md:337, C249's R3 residue; `unrestorable_block` is explicitly 'Not a health verdict', casper/src/interpreter_util.rs:431-433). Therefore `ready` can be true for a node that will never reach the anchor.
rows.consequence: Evidence-class deviation: the gate's summary presents a readiness boolean as health. The immediate false PASS is narrow because the gate separately checks `unrestorableRecords` (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:57-65) and, in the proposed fix, the anchor; the residual is the uncounted refusal or stale-fringe case (see HR-EARLY-1), which `ready` cannot see.
rows.current_behaviour: A ready=true node with a stale or refused canonical chain is admitted to the health conjunction; nothing in the record distinguishes inclusion-readiness from safety.
rows.safeguard: State in the gate's code and in the acceptance method that `ready` is necessary and not sufficient, and never use it as the safety conjunct; keep the divergence and anchor checks as the safety predicates. Optionally have the node expose `serving` (inclusion) and `advancing` (finality) as separate fields so a consumer cannot mistake one for the other.
rows.formalizable: No theorem: `ready` is a liveness predicate and no law states 'ready implies safe'. Owed as a method statement: a readiness boolean may not appear in a safety gate; the two conjuncts (inclusion, finality/divergence) are named separately. The current pairing of `ready` and `unrestorableRecords` is already that shape, undocumented.
rows.falsifier: A control where ready=true but the anchor is false must not pass (proves `ready` alone is insufficient); the existing permanent-divergence control (tests/test_recovery_harness_controls.py:129-146) is the counted half.
rows.cost: Documentation plus one control case.

rows.deviation: The divergence gate trusts `unrestorableRecords == 0` but not `finalityCountersDurable`. When the store could not be read or written, the zero is this process's running totals, not the shard's history, so a restarted shard that gave up on a block reads 0 and passes.
rows.cause: `seed_counters` sets `counters_durable = false` on a boot-read error and leaves the three counters at their defaults (casper/src/interpreter_util.rs:329-338); the flag is mapped to the wire (node/src/api/dto.rs:290-294; node/src/api/conversion.rs:139) and the schema states that false means the counters are the process's, not the shard's (node/src/web/http.rs:1498) -> the drill checks only the integer (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:57-59) -> it gates on a value the node itself says is not the shard's history. Separately, `unrestorableBlock` is deliberately not persisted (casper/src/interpreter_util.rs:431-433), so after a restart the PERMANENT_DIVERGENCE details at :61 render `(node, None)`.
rows.consequence: False PASS: a shard with a spent divergence record from before a restart passes the 'no permanent divergence' gate. Secondary evidence loss: the raised error cannot name the block it is about.
rows.current_behaviour: A non-durable zero is accepted as 'no divergence'; the fail-closed rule already used for a missing int (:57) is not applied to the provenance boolean.
rows.safeguard: Apply the same fail-closed rule: require `type(finalityCountersDurable) is bool and finalityCountersDurable is True` alongside `unrestorableRecords == 0`; if false, treat the reading as unknown (retry/raise) and record the flag along with `finalityStallEpisodes`/`nonQuietMergeReports`, which share it. Persist the block id or fold the count-only verdict into the evidence cell.
rows.formalizable: W-N10-02's own wire contract is the statement (dto.rs:290-294, http.rs:1498); no Lean law. Layer on the harness, with the durable flag already shipped as the node-side R2.
rows.falsifier: A control that returns `{unrestorableRecords: 0, finalityCountersDurable: false}` must make the gate return None; the existing missing-counter control (tests/test_recovery_harness_controls.py:108-126) omits the flag entirely.
rows.cost: One boolean read and one control case.

rows.node: Readiness and health signals — permanently latched faults as a wait condition
rows.deviation: The gate treats a permanently latched fault as transient: a nonzero `pipelineFaults` or `proposalHalted` returns None (retry) instead of a named terminal verdict, so one retryable validation fault anywhere in the window makes the gate unpassable and the run ends in a bare 'did not pass within 150s'.
rows.cause: `record_block_fault` calls `note_pipeline_fault` for every retryable Internal failure, including 'missing justification' (casper/src/blocks/block_processor.rs:121-130; other call sites :129, :174, casper/src/blocks/block_receiver.rs:587) -> `PIPELINE_FAULTS` only increments (:44-51) and only a restart or resume clears the latch (the module doc at :64-67 says so); `proposal_isolated` is cleared only by `clear_proposal_isolation` (casper/src/blocks/proposer/proposer.rs:947-957) -> the gate maps both to `return None` (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:69-77) -> the deadline in tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:122-141 expires -> the message names the window, not the latch.
rows.consequence: False FAIL: a correct rejoin is rejected because an unrelated block faulted, and the verdict is lost into a timeout that is then attributed to the harness race. A node merely syncing (ready=false while its shard is still NodeSyncing) is conflated with the same retry, extending the false-FAIL surface to a slow-but-correct catch-up.
rows.current_behaviour: All non-healthy readings are the same 'try again' branch; terminal and transient conditions are indistinguishable in the outcome and in the message.
rows.safeguard: Split the predicate: transient (shard not yet Running, a single read error) -> None; terminal latch (`pipelineFaults > 0`, `proposalHalted is True`) -> raise a named error carrying `lastPipelineFault` and `proposalHaltReason`, and record it in the cycle. Keep `ready=false` due to sync on the retry path.
rows.formalizable: Law 51a's shape vocabulary: a latched fault has no rule that restores it, so it is `Terminal` (`Rchain.System.Terminal`), whereas the deadline applies the `Drift` disposition (bound the rate). The law names the shapes; the fix is to dispatch on the shape rather than collapse both into a deadline.
rows.falsifier: A control whose mocked /health reports `pipelineFaults: 1` on every poll must raise `PIPELINE_FAULTED` naming `lastPipelineFault`; today it would fall through to the wait's timeout.
rows.cost: A three-way verdict taxonomy and two control cases.

rows.node: Readiness and health signals — the healing gate's health conjunct (/health + /api/v1/status/operator)
rows.deviation: The gate never reads the finality-stall alarm. It records `finalityStall` (the nullable per-observation diagnosis that the schema explicitly calls 'NOT an alarm') and omits `finalityStalled` and `finalityStallEpisodes`, so a node in a sustained finality stall passes the health gate.
rows.cause: The operator DTO carries both fields: `finality_stall` (dto.rs:278) and `finality_stalled` (dto.rs:282), with the wire descriptions saying 'read finalityStalled for that' (node/src/web/http.rs:1495-1497); the mapping is correct (node/src/api/conversion.rs:136-138) -> the drill's status dict reads only `operator.get("finalityStall")` (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:50) -> the predicate at :69-77 tests ready/orphans/faults/halt and never the stall flag -> a stalled node's `is_finalized(B*)` is still true for any anchor at or below its last published fringe, because `finalized_blocks_set` is the seen-closure of the latest fringe (block-storage/src/dag/representation.rs:61-67,141-143; casper/src/api/block_api_impl.rs:1120-1125) -> the proposed fixed anchor passes on a node that has stopped advancing.
rows.consequence: False PASS: a node that entered a sustained stall after reaching the anchor is certified as healed. It is also an evidence loss: the one field that distinguishes 'stalled now' from 'healthy' is absent from the probe record, so the 150s timeout is misdiagnosed as a moving-head race (the failure under review).
rows.current_behaviour: Gate passes on a stalled node; the recorded `finality_stall` string is normally non-null on a healthy producing chain (its own docs say so, node/src/web/http.rs:1495-1497), so its presence proves nothing either way.
rows.safeguard: Require `finalityStalled is False` for every node, fail closed on a missing or non-bool value, record `finalityStalled`/`finalityStallEpisodes` beside `finalityStall`, and put the boolean plus the reason string into the timeout message. Bound: the flag is process state, so sample it in the same pass as the anchor (see HR-BEFORE-1).
rows.formalizable: No Lean law. The node-side protection is shipped R2: F-U18-09 put `finalityStalled`/`finalityStallEpisodes` on the peer-facing /health route (node/src/web/http.rs:766-767; HAZOP F-U18-09). The deviation is that the acceptance harness ignores the field the on-node protection produces; it is a layer, not a node theorem.
rows.falsifier: A control that returns `{finalityStalled: true}` with matching anchors must make `finalized_marker_agreement` return None or raise; the current unit fixture (tests/test_recovery_harness_controls.py:73-90) never puts the key in the health dict, so it would still pass today.
rows.cost: One extra field read per node per poll and one control case; no node change.

rows.node: Readiness and health signals — the health read and the anchor read are two separate passes
rows.deviation: The health snapshot and the anchor reading are separate passes, and the gate returns success from the later one; a node that becomes unhealthy between them is accepted. The advertised 150s bound is also not an end bound: the deadline is checked only at the loop top, after which the condition runs and its result is accepted.
rows.cause: `finalized_marker_agreement` reads /health and the operator status for all 8 nodes (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:37-56), then calls `finalized_marker` (:80), which calls `snapshot()` (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:143-145,84-94) to re-read status and last-finalized, then probes 8 nodes (:152); every HTTP call has timeout=10 (:35), so one condition evaluation can take tens of seconds (worst case 8 nodes x 3 calls x 10s). `wait` checks `time.monotonic() < deadline` only before calling the condition and returns its value without re-checking (:122-141), so a condition that starts before 150s and finishes after it still PASSes.
rows.consequence: False PASS: a momentarily healthy overlap is enough; a node that faults or isolates after the health read but before/while the anchor is read is certified. Evidence defect: the failure text says 'within 150s' though elapsed can exceed it, so the record's timing is not the bound it claims.
rows.current_behaviour: One-shot snapshots of two different states, joined by the caller's ordering; the deadline bounds the start of a check, not its completion.
rows.safeguard: Fold the health and anchor reads for node i into one per-node function in the same pass, require the pair to hold on k >= 2 consecutive samples (a dwell) with the two sample timestamps recorded, and enforce the deadline after the condition as well (compute and report real elapsed). Bind k and the read budget by measurement: k * (per-node read cost) < window.
rows.formalizable: A layer: no node theorem; the shape is a split read (the harness analogue of law 73's one-lock section). Owed harness predicate: `confirmed(phi) := phi on k consecutive samples`, with the sample period measured rather than assumed.
rows.falsifier: A control where the mocked health turns bad on the second read while the anchors stay good must not produce a PASS; with the single-pass/dwell rule it returns None. A second control with a condition that sleeps past the deadline must not PASS.
rows.cost: Restructure the condition into one per-node function and add a dwell constant; two control tests.

rows.node: Readiness and health signals — the proposed fixed anchor can be satisfied by a pre-partition fringe
rows.deviation: The proposed anchor can be satisfied before the evidence it exists to certify exists. `is_finalized(B*)` is answered from the node's own latest-fringe seen-closure, so a victim that never reconnected still answers true for any B* at or below its pre-partition finalized height. H* = min among the seven online is not guaranteed to exceed the victim's own height, and the drill never records the victim's height at partition install.
rows.cause: `before` is read from node 0 only (tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:154) and the online-progress loop reads nodes 0..6 (:167-171), so the victim's (node 7's) pre-partition finalized height is never measured; the proposed H* is a minimum over the online set; `is_finalized` is membership in `finalized_blocks_set`, the seen-closure of the latest fringe (block-storage/src/dag/representation.rs:61-67,141-143; casper/src/api/block_api_impl.rs:1120-1125), a purely local and monotone predicate -> a disconnected victim whose own finalized height >= H* answers true with no post-partition block -> `finalized_marker(H*)` only requires the local head to be >= H* (tools/consensus-acceptance-drill.py:150) -> every predicate can be true while no reconnection occurred. The `docker network connect` at :182 proves the namespace changed, not that the node received anything.
rows.consequence: False PASS of the arm's own property: the rejoin witness is satisfied by the pre-partition state. In run 41208692673 the victim was below H* (56 vs 67), so the hole did not fire; that is a measured coincidence, not a guard.
rows.current_behaviour: The anchor proves 'this node had finalized B* at some point', which is implied by the pre-partition state; it does not prove catch-up or reconnection.
rows.safeguard: Require evidence produced after the partition: record the victim's finalized height at install (`victim_before`) and require is-finalized true for a block whose height > victim_before (equivalently, require the victim's last-finalized height to exceed victim_before and the anchor to be above it). Choose H* from the max or median of the online set (the existing `target = max(...)` at :183 already does this), assert the online spread is within a measured bound, and do not use the minimum.
rows.formalizable: Owed law (candidate `REJOIN-EVIDENCE`): a rejoin witness must cite a block whose height exceeds the witness node's finalized height at partition install. Witness: the state in which the victim holds B* from before the partition and has received no post-partition block, which the current predicate accepts; the law would forbid it. This is owed, not a layer of the node — the node's `is_finalized` is honest about its own fringe; the harness draws a stronger inference than the predicate supports.
rows.falsifier: A drill arm that installs the partition and never reconnects (or connects but drops all traffic) with H* at or below the victim's height: the current gate passes; the post-partition-height rule rejects it.
rows.cost: One extra read at install, a stored baseline, one assertion; one arm.

rows.node: U-CH chain dynamics: workload driver, in-flight deploys, block production, catch-up rate, merge search cost
rows.deviation: The proposed fixed anchor can be a block the victim already stored before the partition. H* is the `min` of the seven survivors' `last-finalized` heights taken at healing start; nothing ties H* to the partition, and nothing compares it with the victim's own DAG. `is_finalized(B*)` is then satisfied by pre-partition history, so the drill certifies a rejoin the victim never performed.
rows.cause: `last_finalized_block` is not 'the newest finalized block': it is `max_by_key(|m| (m.height, m.id))` over the *carried* fringe of whichever latest message carries the freshest fringe (`block-storage/src/dag/representation.rs:77-81`, `block-storage/src/dag/message_map.rs:70-89`, `block-storage/src/dag/message_state.rs:437-440`), a projection whose lag behind the tip is unbounded and that the drill never measures. The partition is installed after reading only *node 0's* fence (`tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:154`) and the victim's own finalized height at that instant is never recorded, so no code point can compare H* with it. `is_finalized` is membership in the seen-closure of the latest fringe (`representation.rs:62-66`, `:141-143`); every block at or below the victim's pre-partition fence is in that closure.
rows.consequence: FALSE PASS, S1. On the reported run's shape (anchor 48, victim reported at 56 at healing start) all eight would answer true on the first poll, before one partition-era block was replayed, and `finalized_marker(48, required=True)` also passes because it compares each node's own fence height. The victim would remain outside the live set (`LIVENESS_WINDOW = 5`, `block-storage/src/dag/liveness.rs:51`) and would never attest, yet `PASS_BOUNDED_WORKLOAD_PARTITION_REJOIN` (`tests/consensus-partition-rejoin.py:204`) would be written. The drill's own stated scope ('retention and finality progression', same line) does not cover this, but the check is described as 'all validators agree ... after partition healing', which is what becomes false.
rows.current_behaviour: The predicate is satisfiable from history, and the drill has no lower bound on the anchor.
rows.safeguard: Choose B* only from a block with `blockNumber > victim_finalized_height_at_partition_install` (read `/api/block/{hash}` and check `blockNumber`; record `victim_before` in the cycle record). If the min over the seven does not strictly exceed that floor, fail as `ANCHOR_PREDATES_PARTITION` instead of passing. The bound is exact (a height comparison), not a tolerance.
rows.formalizable: Owed law `rejoin_certificate_is_outside_the_certified_node's_prefix`: for every node n and certificate block b, `b ∈ finalized(n) ⇒ ¬ reachable(prefix_victim, b)`; witness: two DAGs agreeing on a prefix P with b ∈ P and b outside the contended suffix.
rows.falsifier: Offline control: feed `finalized_marker_agreement` a victim whose DAG already contains B* and never advances; it must return None. Live: after reconnect, block the victim's block requests so it cannot catch up — the drill must fail, not pass at poll 1.
rows.cost: One `/api/block/{hash}` read per cycle plus one recorded integer; one new negative-control test.

rows.node: U-CH chain dynamics: workload driver, in-flight deploys, block production, catch-up rate, merge search cost
